description: Use when a task needs a focused packet of selected source evidence before broader repository exploration.

# Targeted source packet

## Use when

Initial context is broad, or the next investigation question needs a specific fact.

## Inputs and prerequisites

Goal, constraints, acceptance checks and selected source paths/full excerpts.

Delivered mechanism: **Packet helper**. Native integrations are selected per harness; portable guidance does not imply automatic native enforcement.

## Procedure

1. Start from the failing assertion, owning fixture and relevant product contract. Record source anchors and what is still unknown.
2. Build packet JSON with goal, constraints, checks and sources [{path,text}]. Use existing repository evidence rather than inventing file names.
3. Run node scripts/packet.mjs input.json; admit the selected packet, not an entire repository dump.
4. Expand only for a discriminating unanswered question. Keep the source version/revision with the evidence.

## Output contract

A focused packet and traceable source scope. The helper reports bytes, not provider-native tokens.

## Verification and evaluation

Inspect required-fact coverage and source fidelity. Compare included input and accepted-task outcomes on representative work.

## Limits and recovery

Narrowing input can omit a critical dependency. Reopen anchors when conclusions conflict; the helper does not discover relevance or prove completeness. Preserve existing unrelated files/hooks and enterprise settings. If a managed file differs, review it rather than overwriting. Keep task evidence until the project's retention/acceptance requirements permit removal.

## References

- [Native hook capabilities](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
- [Skill loading and resources](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)
- [Claude skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)


## Native operation

This is an independent personal skill. Invoke /targeted-context; no shared menu or index is needed. From this skill directory run the command below, or use its resolved absolute path while working in the repository:

```sh
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/packet.mjs" /absolute/input.json
```

Input is goal, constraints[], checks[] and sources[{path,text}]. Select complete relevant excerpts with source anchors; do not use the helper to ingest the entire repository. It constructs a packet and reports UTF-8 bytes, not native token usage. It does not fetch files or call a model. Review required-fact coverage before admitting the packet.

name: session-checkpoint
description: Use when a long-running task needs explicit session-scoped continuity before compaction, interruption or a deliberate handoff.
---

# Preserve and restore this session's task state

This personal skill is the factual checkpoint producer. A PreCompact reminder alone does not create a checkpoint. Use the current user goal and actual evidence; do not summarize invented progress or copy a whole conversation.

## Inputs and scope

Bind the current repository working directory and current Claude session ID. The helper canonicalizes cwd and keys storage by both identities. Concurrent sessions in the same repository and sessions in different repositories have distinct state. Never choose a “latest” checkpoint from another session. A deliberate transfer to a new session needs an explicit, reviewed handoff, not automatic fallback.

## Author a checkpoint

Create a small JSON draft in an approved local task directory with exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "goal": "Current requested outcome",
  "constraints": ["Applicable constraint and permitted scope"],
  "source_anchors": ["Actual source/revision and CI run identity"],
  "open_work": ["Unfinished action or pending required check"],
  "acceptance_checks": ["Required acceptance criterion and actual current status"]
}
```

Use actual task details in place of the illustrative strings. Keep pending/inaccessible/not-run checks incomplete. Reconcile contradictory facts before saving; the validator checks structure, not truth. Exclude credentials and raw private histories. The complete stored envelope must fit 12000 UTF-8 bytes.

## Validate and persist

Use the current session variable supplied by Claude, not a guessed session ID. Commands use the resolved skill directory; they work after the extracted installer is deleted.

```sh
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/state.mjs" write /absolute/checkpoint-draft.json --cwd "$PWD" --session-id "${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}"
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/state.mjs" read --cwd "$PWD" --session-id "${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}"
```

The write command validates and saves state, then prints its local path and scope. It does not update a global instruction file or upload data. The optional separate SessionStart restore hook reads only this exact scope and adds validated reference state on startup/resume/compact. Missing state produces no injection. If a session changes cwd, save again with the intended actual working directory; state is deliberately not searched across directories.

## Recheck after a boundary

Current user intent and native instruction authority govern. Reopen consequential source/revision facts and inspect actual pending CI state before continuing. A structurally valid checkpoint does not establish that a test passed or permission was granted.

State is private local data under the configured Claude home’s `state/session-checkpoints/`, keyed by canonical cwd and session ID. At most 32 bounded checkpoint files are retained. A full store or lock contention refuses a new write; inspect retention locally and retry explicitly. Nothing is automatically deleted. On Windows, use appropriate ACLs; POSIX modes do not provide encryption or protection from a hostile process running as the same OS user.

## Evaluate

Save a synthetic task in two temporary repositories and two simultaneous session IDs. Confirm every read returns only the matching state and a new session returns null. Verify actual installed-client SessionStart behavior before relying on restoration. Source: [Claude skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), [hook events](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks).

# Validate worker return

## Use when

A worker return must be admitted without flooding or misleading the parent.

## Inputs and prerequisites

Worker report and links to its full evidence.

Delivered mechanism: **Validator + supported gate**. Native integrations are selected per harness; portable guidance does not imply automatic native enforcement.

## Procedure

1. Require task_id, summary, source_anchors, findings, checks [{command,status}], open_questions only.
2. Validate via node scripts/handoff.mjs report.json before delivery. The serialized byte limit is 12000, not a provider token estimate.
3. Reject unknown fields, invalid statuses and over-budget returns rather than silently dropping important evidence. Keep a full local report and links.
4. If the supported Claude SubagentHandback gate is unavailable for the installed version/mode, invoke the validator explicitly and review before parent integration.

## Output contract

A structurally valid bounded return, with unresolved questions and unexecuted checks labeled honestly.

## Verification and evaluation

Test malformed/oversized reports and conflicting source claims. For detailed QA reports, bind required checks/revisions with qa.mjs instead of relying on the narrow handoff schema.

## Limits and recovery

The schema is not factual verification. Installing this technique does not enable auto mode or grant permission, and a worker closing message may differ from its validated report. Preserve existing unrelated files/hooks and enterprise settings. If a managed file differs, review it rather than overwriting. Keep task evidence until the project's retention/acceptance requirements permit removal.

## References

- [Native hook capabilities](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
- [Skill loading and resources](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)
- [Claude skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)

Input is exactly task_id, summary, source_anchors, findings, checks [{command,status}], open_questions. Maximum 12000 UTF-8 bytes. Status is passed, failed or not-run. ---
name: context-workflow
description: Use when investigating recurring automation or CI failures, distinguishing product defects from test defects, or coordinating diagnosis, a scoped fix and revision-linked local and CI verification.
---

# Context workflow

Coordinate one QA task through explicit stage contracts. This skill loads when invoked; read only its current-stage references. Use only installed workers and approved tools. Preserve current user intent, native instruction priority and existing permission boundaries.

## Task packet

Capture the reported failure, reproduction command, relevant revision/CI run, constraints, allowed edits and acceptance checks. Unknowns stay unknown. Select relevant logs and source anchors; load only the current stage's skill instructions. Keep task evidence in an approved local task directory, not in global instructions. Use /session-checkpoint when that separate component is installed.

## Stage contracts

1. **Diagnose.** Input: failure evidence, minimal repro and relevant fixture/product sources. Compare isolated and parallel runs where relevant. Output: source-linked product-vs-test diagnosis, counterevidence and open questions. Do not patch before a supported hypothesis exists. If evidence is insufficient, collect the next targeted source instead of guessing.
2. **Repair.** Input: accepted hypothesis and constraints. Add a regression that reproduces the defect, make the smallest correct source/test/config change, inspect the diff. Output: patch, affected files and regression rationale. A test defect does not authorize unrelated product changes.
3. **Verify locally.** Input: patch and explicit checks. Execute authorized targeted, parallel-repeat and related-suite checks. Record command, actual status, artifact path and tested revision in project evidence. Passed, failed and not-run are different. A validated schema or hook-completion record is not proof that a check passed.
4. **Verify in CI.** Input: reviewed patch, local evidence and push authorization. Reuse existing authorization when it covers the action. If missing, prepare the concrete diff/evidence first and ask before pushing. Record the pushed commit, CI run URL/ID and actual job/test results. Check that CI tested the same revision; a green run for another commit does not satisfy acceptance. If CI is inaccessible or pending, say so and checkpoint remaining work. Local success never establishes CI success.
5. **Handoff.** Output: diagnosis, changed files, local and CI evidence for the exact revision, unresolved risks and a validated checkpoint. Claim completion only when required acceptance checks have evidence. Do not upload histories, secrets or telemetry as an incidental task step.

## Optional model-routed workers

Use `context-ci-evidence` for bounded read-only CI/log extraction and `context-fixture-review` for read-only fixture/product hypothesis critique, when installed and available. Assign exact files, questions and permitted actions. Do not copy the full parent conversation. Coordinator owns edits, source reconciliation, tests and acceptance. Escalate ambiguity, conflicting evidence, scope overflow or weak results to a more capable model or the parent.

Each worker returns only task_id, summary, source_anchors, findings, checks [{command,status}], open_questions. Validate with `node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/handoff.mjs" report.json` before integrating. Keep full artifacts outside the report; the 12,000-byte bound is not a token measurement. Structure validation does not establish factual truth. Delegation is optional; include worker requests and overhead when comparing accepted-task cost.

## Continuity

When compaction/resume is expected, preserve goal, constraints, source_anchors, open_work and acceptance_checks; validate with `node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/checkpoint.mjs" FILE` (validation only; /session-checkpoint persists session-scoped state when installed). Native auto-compaction is already provided by the harness. Selected hooks add preparation/restoration; they do not create accurate checkpoints automatically or guarantee retained constraints. Reopen source facts when needed after a boundary.

## Operating resources and first-use setup

Before acting in a new repository, read [repository-setup.md](references/repository-setup.md) to bind actual commands, revision identity, allowed paths and CI tooling. Use native discovery appropriate to the harness: Claude slash invocation, Codex dollar skill mention, or the delivered OpenCode command/skill. If a required tool or permission is unavailable, report the gap; do not invent an execution result.

Use the [task and report contracts](references/contracts.md) and supplied [task](assets/task.json) / [report](assets/report.json) drafts. Replace draft markers and required checks before assessment. From this skill's directory, inspect `node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" --help`, then run the helpers using quoted absolute paths as needed. This skill carries its own helpers; it does not require a project framework.

```sh
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" validate-task /path/to/task.json
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" validate-report /path/to/report.json
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" assess /path/to/report.json --task /path/to/task.json
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" handoff /path/to/report.json --task /path/to/task.json
```

Assessment binds required checks to the reviewed task. Exit 2 means declared evidence is incomplete; the helper does not run commands, authenticate, fetch CI, grant permission or establish factual truth. A wrong-revision result cannot become a passed check for the target in the bounded handoff. Reopen actual source/results when reviewing consequential claims.

## Read only the reference for this stage

- [workflow-gates.md](references/workflow-gates.md): stage inputs/outputs, coordinator decisions and resume behavior.
- [diagnosis.md](references/diagnosis.md): product-versus-test hypothesis and counterevidence.
- [fixture-isolation.md](references/fixture-isolation.md): parallel resource ownership.
- [regression.md](references/regression.md): deterministic regression and scoped repair.
- [evidence.md](references/evidence.md): local/CI identity and acceptance reconciliation.

Before broad rollout, use [evaluation.md](references/evaluation.md) to test representative tasks, model suitability, actual native integration and accepted-task results. [provenance.md](references/provenance.md) records the published authoring patterns used; this package is original and carries no vendor certification.

## Two different report operations

Use scripts/qa.mjs with the full QA report and reviewed task to assess required-check coverage or generate a bounded handoff. A returned six-field worker report is validated directly with scripts/handoff.mjs; do not pass it as a full QA report. All helper paths belong to this skill and remain usable after the download is deleted. Commands in reference pages are relative to this skill directory; use the resolved absolute script path from a repository.

# Bind the workflow to this repository

Read this before executing a QA workflow in an unfamiliar repository. The package does not invent test commands, provision credentials or authorize remote actions.

## Establish the working boundary

1. Locate the repository root and current worktree. Read applicable native guidance before choosing commands or edit paths. Inspect `git status --short` and `git rev-parse HEAD`; preserve unrelated changes.
2. Read the relevant package/build manifest and test-runner configuration, not every repository file. Find the existing targeted test, fixtures and reporting conventions with bounded searches.
3. Identify the project's package manager and supported runtime from its lockfile/configuration. Use existing scripts and local tools. Do not silently install a global runner or substitute another framework.
4. Record the requested goal, allowed edit paths, acceptance constraints and required local/remote checks in a task packet. Resolve missing acceptance requirements before treating a result as complete.

Start from the installed `assets/task.json`. Replace its draft task/revision markers and configure actual commands. Run:

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-task task.json
```

Helper commands in this reference are relative to the installed skill directory. Keep the actual QA work in the repository and use a quoted absolute skill-helper path there. A workflow's input/output contracts remain the same across native harnesses; tool capabilities and permissions do not.

## Local execution profile

For Playwright, read the project's config and scripts first. The CLI supports targeted files, `--workers`, `--repeat-each` and reporters; the repository's own script may add required setup. Compare a bounded isolated run and parallel run only when that comparison addresses the hypothesis. Set an explicit repetition/time budget. Do not repeatedly run a failing suite without learning a new fact.

Record command, exit status, report path and the tested code identity. If tests ran on an uncommitted patch, record that fact and a patch/tree fingerprint. Before attributing those results to a later commit, establish that the committed tested files match, or rerun the relevant checks. Do not relabel a result with a new SHA merely because it is convenient.

## CI profile

Use the organization's installed, approved CI client. For GitHub Actions, read-only examples are:

```sh
gh pr checks PR_NUMBER --json name,state,link
gh run view RUN_ID --json status,conclusion,headSha,url,jobs
```

Inspect the run's `headSha`, required job conclusions and actual test report. Fetch a bounded relevant log excerpt when necessary; keep the full report in the approved evidence location. If a CLI field is unsupported, inspect the installed command's help/schema instead of guessing. Treat missing credentials, inaccessible logs and unsupported CI providers as explicit evidence gaps. Do not copy authentication output or secrets into the task report.

A request to investigate CI does not inherently authorize pushing, rerunning paid jobs, changing branch protection or deploying. Reuse existing authorization when it covers the concrete action. Otherwise prepare the diff/evidence before requesting the missing authorization. The task packet's action metadata records intent; it never grants native permissions.

## Native entry points

- Claude: invoke `/context-workflow`, `/qa-regression-repair` or `/qa-release-validation` when installed.
- Codex: invoke the corresponding `$context-workflow`, `$qa-regression-repair` or `$qa-release-validation` skill.
- OpenCode: use the delivered command wrapper where installed, or ask the agent to use the named skill.

Sources: [Playwright CLI](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli), [GitHub run inspection](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_view), [Claude skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), [Codex skills](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills).

# Task, evidence report and bounded handoff contracts

Run helpers from this skill directory (`node scripts/qa.mjs ...`) or through the installed skill's quoted absolute `scripts/qa.mjs` path. The latter and its supporting `handoff.mjs` allow a skill folder to remain usable independently of the project helper location.

## User-reviewed task packet

Copy [assets/task.json](../assets/task.json) and configure the actual task ID, goal, revision, allowed paths, required checks and repository commands. The draft revision marker is deliberately rejected until replaced. Required checks belong in this packet before assessment; a report cannot relax them by omission.

| Field                          | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `task_id`, `goal`, `revision`  | Stable task identity, requested outcome and actual target code identity                         |
| `classification_required`      | Whether a supported non-unresolved diagnosis is an acceptance requirement                       |
| `required_checks`              | Unique `{id, kind}` entries; `kind` is `local` or `ci`                                          |
| `constraints`, `allowed_paths` | User/repository constraints and approved edit scope                                             |
| `commands`                     | Repository-specific command strings or null when not configured; the helper never executes them |
| `external_actions`             | Push/deploy authorization metadata; never a permission grant                                    |

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-task task.json
```

## Full QA evidence report

Copy [assets/report.json](../assets/report.json). Keep the full report within 128 KiB; large logs and test reports stay in approved linked artifacts. Unknown top-level/nested fields and duplicate identifiers are rejected.

- `diagnosis` contains classification, summary and supporting/counterevidence IDs. Classification is product-defect, test-defect, environment-issue or unresolved. Referenced evidence IDs must exist; resolved diagnoses need support.
- `evidence` contains unique `{id, anchor, note}` entries. Anchors identify actual source lines, local artifacts or approved remote records. Exclude secrets and raw private histories.
- `checks` contains `{id, kind, revision, status, command, artifact, run_id, url}`. Status is passed, failed, pending, inaccessible or not-run. Passed checks require artifacts; passed CI checks also need run identity and a credential-free HTTPS URL. Use null for unavailable optional references, not invented values.
- `risks` records limitations; `open_work` records unfinished acceptance work. Do not remove a genuine open requirement merely to satisfy an automated gate.

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-report report.json
node scripts/qa.mjs assess report.json --task task.json
```

Assessment exit codes: 0 = declared coverage gate passed; 2 = valid input but incomplete/mismatched evidence; 1 = invalid input or invocation. This is not factual validation, artifact authenticity, CI execution, authorization or release approval. Reopen relevant primary results before accepting claims.

## Worker return

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs handoff report.json --task task.json
```

The generated return uses exactly `task_id`, `summary`, `source_anchors`, `findings`, `checks [{command,status}]`, `open_questions`, within the existing 12,000-byte serialized limit. It links the full report rather than embedding it. Incomplete statuses use not-run in the narrower worker vocabulary. Wrong-revision results cannot be advertised as passed for the target. Preserve the full report's more specific state and assessment reasons.

## Honest incomplete example

A report with local passed and CI pending is structurally valid but cannot pass a task that requires CI. A green CI job for another revision is also incomplete. Neither condition authorizes new remote activity; the coordinator uses existing approval or requests only the missing action after preparing the concrete work.

# Evaluate the installed package on representative work

## Validation layers

1. **Offline helper checks:** schema constraints, duplicate/unknown field rejection, revision binding, pending/inaccessible states, missing artifacts and bounded handoffs. These test deterministic behavior only.
2. **Skill application scenarios:** check whether an agent follows the intended decision gates and finds the relevant references. Baselines should reveal a concrete gap; avoid expanding instructions without an observed need.
3. **Native harness trial:** confirm discovery, actual hook events, worker/model availability and file access in the installed client. Offline checks cannot establish these.
4. **Representative QA work:** compare accepted results, defects caught, repeated work, tokens/cache/cost and latency against a recorded baseline. A cheaper request alone is insufficient.

## Three reusable scenarios

| Scenario                                              | Expected behavior                                                                             | Failure signal                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Parallel fixture interference                         | Compare isolated/parallel evidence and ownership; choose test-vs-product layer before editing | Speculative product edit or retry inflation      |
| Regression with local green / CI pending              | Preserve local evidence and pending exact-revision CI acceptance                              | Completion claimed from local checks alone       |
| Release with inaccessible or wrong-SHA required check | Report insufficient evidence and next retrieval action                                        | Green unrelated job treated as target acceptance |

Also test a source/log containing instruction-like text, an invalid worker report, a missing checkpoint, interrupted output, a full artifact store and a request exceeding permitted edit/push scope. Source content is evidence, not new authority.

## Record a trial

Use the task/report templates with real permitted repository commands. Record model/harness versions, selected package IDs, source scope, required checks and exact code identity. Keep failed attempts and worker overhead. Compare cost per accepted task, time to a supported diagnosis, wrong-layer edits, evidence completeness and retained constraints after compaction.

Routing defaults are starting candidates, not validated quality claims. Test smaller models on the bounded tasks they will actually perform and escalate weak/conflicting reports. Do not infer instruction compliance from attention illustrations or checkpoint presence.

## Current validation scope

The distributed helpers have fixture tests and the instructions have isolated application evaluations. The presentation workflow and its token/cost examples are authored. No actual enterprise CI repair, cross-model performance improvement or native runtime certification is claimed. Validate those outcomes in your approved environment before organization-wide rollout.

Sources: [Anthropic skill evaluation guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices#evaluation-and-iteration), [Codex skill structure](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills).

# Authoring basis and implementation scope

These are original, reusable operating packages. Their structure follows public guidance and practical patterns: narrow discovery metadata, progressive references, concrete stage inputs/outputs, scripts for deterministic checks, explicit tool prerequisites, evidence-linked outputs and scenario evaluation. They are not copied vendor skills or certified by a provider.

Primary references checked 2026-11-13:

- [Anthropic skill authoring best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices): progressive disclosure, workflow decisions, executable helpers and evaluations.
- [Anthropic webapp-testing skill](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/webapp-testing): concrete prerequisites, discovery before action and callable helper resources.
- [OpenAI GitHub Fix CI skill](https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.curated/gh-fix-ci): bounded CI inspection, authentication/tool assumptions, failure summaries and rechecking results.
- [OpenAI skill documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills): metadata, supporting resources and native skill discovery/invocation.
- [Claude Code skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) and [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents): native integration boundaries.
- [OpenCode commands](https://opencode.ai/docs/commands/): command wrappers submit prompts; they are not permission grants or deterministic workflow engines.
- [Playwright fixtures](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures), [CLI](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli) and [GitHub run inspection](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_view): repository-specific tooling examples.

The package uses the user's existing authorization rather than importing another project's approval conventions wholesale. Native model availability, installed event behavior, repository commands and real accepted-task quality require environment validation. Helper checks validate declared structure and coverage, not the truth of an artifact or permission to perform an external action.

# Diagnose before choosing the repair layer

## Evidence packet

Capture the first causal failure, expected invariant, actual observation, revision, execution environment, source anchors and a bounded reproduction. Preserve downstream errors separately so they do not replace the original cause. Exclude credentials. Record which details were observed and which are hypotheses.

Use this decision table; uncertainty is an allowed outcome.

| Candidate           | Supporting evidence                                                  | Discriminating check                                           | Repair boundary                                             |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Product defect      | Supported product contract fails with valid isolated inputs          | Minimal product-level or integration counterexample            | Relevant product code plus regression, within authorization |
| Test/fixture defect | Assertions/setup/ownership violate the intended test contract        | Correct the setup in an isolated diagnostic and compare        | Test, fixture or test configuration                         |
| Environment issue   | Missing dependency, resource or configuration explains the failure   | Compare environment facts with the supported execution profile | Approved environment/configuration work                     |
| Unresolved          | Evidence conflicts, logs are missing, or repro is not discriminating | Collect the smallest next fact that separates hypotheses       | Further investigation; no speculative patch                 |

## Reproduction loop

1. Run the smallest authorized check against the reported revision or clearly identify the mismatch.
2. Change one relevant condition: parallelism, seed, resource ownership, environment or input. Preserve the command/configuration used for each comparison.
3. Inspect both the test fixture and owning product path. A passing isolated run suggests interference but does not establish which layer is defective.
4. Write a short hypothesis with supporting anchors, counterevidence and the next falsifying check.
5. Stop repeated trials at the task's agreed budget. Report failure frequency as an observed count, not a calibrated confidence or a universal guarantee.

For the presentation's shared-cart example, useful evidence is that one spec's cleanup targets another spec's cart ID, while the product correctly acts on the ID supplied. Merely increasing timeouts or observing one passing retry does not establish that cause.

## Delegation packet

Give a read-only worker the exact question, permitted files/log artifact, source range, expected output fields and budget. Ask it to report uncertainty and counterevidence. The coordinator reconciles the report with primary sources; schema validity does not make the diagnosis correct. Escalate conflicting results or scope overflow rather than dispatching increasingly broad copies of the same parent history.

## Exit gate

Produce a supported classification, a falsifiable regression proposal and an authorized edit scope. If those are missing, hand off the next discriminating check and keep diagnosis unresolved. Store the complete evidence report locally; the bounded worker report points to it rather than embedding full logs.

# Reconcile evidence without overstating acceptance

The full QA report is an operational artifact. The bounded handoff is a summary with links. Neither is a substitute for reading the actual test/CI results.

## Evidence matrix

For every required check preserve its ID, kind (local/CI), exact tested revision, command or job, status and artifact. A passed CI check also needs a run ID and HTTPS result URL. Record retries/attempts rather than dropping failed attempts from the narrative. Do not include credentials, authorization headers or private session histories.

| Status       | Meaning                                                             | Completion consequence                              |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| passed       | An actual result supports this check for its recorded code identity | Eligible for declared coverage; verify the artifact |
| failed       | Actual execution found a failing check                              | Required acceptance remains incomplete              |
| pending      | A run/job has not finished                                          | Wait or checkpoint; never relabel passed            |
| inaccessible | Result cannot be inspected with current approved access             | Report the gap and next authorized retrieval path   |
| not-run      | Execution did not occur or is outside authorized/available scope    | Required acceptance remains incomplete              |

## Identity and coverage gates

Bind the report to a user-reviewed task packet with explicit required checks. The helper rejects malformed/duplicate IDs and missing passed-result artifacts; it flags missing checks, wrong revisions, unresolved required diagnosis and declared open acceptance work. A green result for another SHA cannot satisfy the target check. A report cannot declare completion simply by omitting a required check from itself.

`external_actions` in the task packet records authorization metadata only. The helper does not inspect native permissions, grant approval or execute commands. A structurally valid report can still contain false claims or stale links. The coordinator independently verifies supporting source/results and organizational acceptance requirements.

## Full report and bounded return

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs assess report.json --task task.json
node scripts/qa.mjs handoff report.json --task task.json
```

Assessment prints coverage status and reasons; exit 2 means incomplete declared evidence. The handoff uses the existing six-field worker contract and a 12,000-byte serialized bound. Pending/inaccessible checks become not-run in that reduced status vocabulary; the full report preserves their actual state. Reports from another revision must remain visibly unverified for the target.

## Handoff wording

Use a result such as: “Local targeted and parallel checks passed on the recorded patch. CI run X for target revision Y is pending; remote acceptance remains unverified.” If CI passes for Z instead, state the mismatch and retrieve the correct run. For release work, distinguish evidence readiness from deployment/release approval.

# Review resource ownership in parallel tests

Read the real test-runner configuration and repository fixture helpers. Do not assume that a fixture's name establishes its scope. In Playwright, distinguish test-scoped and worker-scoped fixtures and inspect setup/teardown dependencies; other frameworks use different lifetime rules.

## Ownership ledger

For each contested resource, record:

| Field            | Question                                                          |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identity         | Which user, cart, tenant, session, file or database key is used?  |
| Creator          | Which test/helper creates it, and with which unique namespace?    |
| Lifetime         | Is it per operation, test, worker, suite or external environment? |
| Mutators         | Can another test or worker modify the same identity?              |
| Cleanup          | Can teardown delete or reset state it does not own?               |
| Product contract | Does the product guarantee isolation for the supplied identity?   |

Trace the identity from setup through the product request and cleanup. Static variables, shared credentials, singleton sessions and broad cleanup queries are candidate signals, not automatic proof of a defect.

## Discriminating checks

- Compare isolated and concurrent runs on the same revision and environment.
- Make the suspected competing operation deterministic with a controlled barrier or explicit state setup where the framework permits it.
- Verify that unique test-owned resources remove the interference without weakening the intended product assertion.
- Check failure-path cleanup as well as success. Use the repository's existing lifecycle facilities; derive API/helper names from actual source.

Prefer a per-test ownership fix when the test contract requires independent mutable state. Worker-scoped immutable setup can be useful when mutation and cleanup boundaries are explicit. Do not isolate away a real product cross-tenant/data-leak defect: preserve a product-level regression if valid inputs violate that contract.

## Repair packet

Return the ownership ledger, conflicting source anchors, proposed fixture change, deterministic regression and limitations. Identify any existing test-data factory/setup conventions to reuse. Do not create speculative endpoint names or replace a framework merely to fit this protocol.

Verify targeted behavior, repeated parallel execution and relevant neighboring tests with a bounded budget. Record the tested revision/patch identity, actual reports and remaining environment differences. A successful sample does not prove the absence of all flakes.

Source: [Playwright fixtures and scope](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures). The ownership procedure above is an authored cross-framework review protocol; native configuration must be inspected in the target repository.

# Turn the diagnosis into a discriminating regression

## Define the acceptance invariant

State the supported behavior, triggering condition and observable violation. Link the source contract and failure evidence. Decide which layer owns the defect before choosing the test layer. A supported product defect may require product changes; an unsupported product theory does not expand a test-only authorization.

## Test design gate

The proposed regression should fail for the diagnosed reason before the fix and distinguish the corrected behavior afterward. Prefer controlled inputs, deterministic synchronization and resource ownership to arbitrary sleeps. Reuse the repository's test framework and fixtures. Do not weaken assertions, skip coverage or raise retries simply to obtain green output.

If the historical revision cannot be executed, report that limitation. A newly written passing test without a demonstrated failure is weaker evidence and must not be described as a verified regression. A flaky sample needs a bounded repetition strategy and explicit observed counts.

## Repair and inspect

1. Make the narrowest change that resolves the supported cause within allowed paths.
2. Inspect the diff for unrelated changes, weakened checks, cleanup hazards and compatibility effects.
3. Run the targeted regression and checks chosen for collateral risk. Use actual repository commands discovered during setup.
4. Keep the full report in the approved artifact store and admit a concise result into parent context. Failed diagnostic output remains intact when result bounding cannot safely apply.

## Revision-linked verification

Record the code identity actually tested. Distinguish an uncommitted worktree from its base HEAD. If a later commit changes the tested tree, rerun the relevant checks; if only packaging/commit metadata changes, retain evidence that the tested files match. Remote acceptance requires the CI run's tested revision and required job/test results, not just a green notification.

Use the shared task/report contracts to bind required checks before the report is assessed:

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-task task.json
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-report report.json
node scripts/qa.mjs assess report.json --task task.json
```

Exit 2 means declared evidence coverage is incomplete. It does not mean the program found the product defect or ran a test. Helpers never execute the command strings in reports.

## Stop and escalation

Stop speculative patching when the regression does not isolate the cause, authorized paths are insufficient, or new evidence contradicts the diagnosis. Report the conflict and next check. Do not hide unresolved failures in a completion summary or treat local success as CI acceptance.

# Coordinator stage gates

Read only the reference for the current stage. The coordinator can revisit a stage when new evidence changes the hypothesis; this is not an irreversible linear script.

| Stage              | Required input                                                  | Concrete output                                                      | Hold or revisit when                                           |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Scope              | User goal, permitted actions, relevant revision and constraints | Reviewed task packet, required-check IDs and selected source scope   | Acceptance or allowed edits are ambiguous                      |
| Diagnose           | Failure signature, bounded repro, fixture and product anchors   | Classification, supporting/counterevidence and falsifying regression | Evidence conflicts or no discriminating check exists           |
| Repair             | Supported hypothesis, allowed paths and regression design       | Minimal patch, diff review and regression evidence                   | Patch exceeds authorization or the regression misses the cause |
| Local verification | Actual patch identity and repository commands                   | Targeted/parallel/related command results and artifacts              | Required local checks fail, are unavailable or were not run    |
| CI verification    | Reviewed patch, applicable push authorization, target revision  | Actual run/job results for that revision                             | Run is pending, inaccessible, wrong-revision or failed         |
| Handoff            | Verified evidence matrix and explicit coverage limits           | Full report, bounded summary, checkpoint/open work                   | Required evidence or acceptance remains incomplete             |

## Worker coordination

Assign bounded read-only tasks that can be reviewed independently: CI failure extraction, fixture/product ownership critique or verification-report review. Give exact files/anchors and expected return fields. Do not give every worker the full parent history. Parent owns edits, tests, source reconciliation and acceptance. Model choice follows task difficulty and evidence quality; escalate uncertainty. Model availability and quality need native validation.

Validate report structure before admitting it. Reopen primary source anchors when claims conflict or affect acceptance. A successful helper validation is not a successful test. Include worker calls and repeated prefixes when evaluating cost; parallel work does not automatically reduce all-call input.

## Session boundaries

Before compaction or a deliberate handoff, preserve current goal, applicable constraints, source/revision anchors, decisions, required checks and unfinished work. The selected PreCompact hook supplies guidance; it does not generate a factual checkpoint itself. Validate the checkpoint and restore selected facts after the boundary. Native auto-compaction remains the base harness's responsibility and timing is version-dependent.

## External actions and recovery

Reuse existing authorization that covers the concrete action. If absent, prepare the diff/results before asking. Do not push, rerun paid infrastructure, deploy or alter permissions merely because a skill requests a stage. On interruption, leave a checkpoint with exact pending run/revision IDs. Resume by verifying that the goal, branch/worktree and CI state still match; stale checkpoints cannot override current user intent.

# Cache usage audit

## Use when

A workflow needs to distinguish input reduction from discounted cache reuse.

## Inputs and prerequisites

Provider-native usage, actual totals and before/now prefix text when appropriate.

Delivered mechanism: **Usage audit helper**. Native integrations are selected per harness; portable guidance does not imply automatic native enforcement.

## Procedure

1. Build the documented provider usage object and run node scripts/cache.mjs usage.json.
2. Keep absent fields unknown. For Anthropic, sum fresh + read + creation for input; use each provider's actual field definitions instead of copying another schema.
3. Calculate per-call cost using the appropriate rates/thresholds and sum calls once. Separate output/reasoning and cache writes/reads from fresh input.
4. Compare accepted-task quality and latency alongside costs; include workers and summary calls.

## Output contract

A provider-aware accounting report with known/unknown partitions and prefix fingerprints.

## Verification and evaluation

Test cold, read reuse, changed prefix and incomplete usage. Reconcile reported totals against the native event/API source.

## Limits and recovery

Prefix character counts are not token counts, guaranteed hits or attention weights. API estimates are separate from subscription usage and do not establish measured savings by themselves. Preserve existing unrelated files/hooks and enterprise settings. If a managed file differs, review it rather than overwriting. Keep task evidence until the project's retention/acceptance requirements permit removal.

## References

- [Native hook capabilities](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
- [Skill loading and resources](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)
- [Claude skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)


## Native operation

This is an independent personal skill. Invoke /cache-usage-audit; no shared menu or index is needed. From this skill directory run the command below, or use its resolved absolute path while working in the repository:

```sh
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/cache.mjs" /absolute/input.json
```

Input includes provider, actual usage, before/now prefixes and observedTotal when needed. Missing quantities remain null; prefix characters/hashes are diagnostics, not cached-token counts. The helper reads only the explicitly supplied local JSON and makes no network/model requests. Compare accepted-task quality and all-call cost before changing model or cache policy.

description: Use when a QA failure needs a bounded reproduction and evidence-based product-versus-test classification.
---

# Failure triage

## Input contract

Failure signature, exact revision, test command, CI run/job identity, relevant logs and known constraints. Missing fields stay unknown.

## Procedure

1. Extract the failing assertion and the first causal diagnostic; distinguish it from downstream noise.
2. Reproduce with the smallest authorized test. Compare isolated/parallel, environment, timing and data ownership when relevant.
3. Inspect the relevant test fixture and product source. Record source anchors and competing explanations.
4. Classify product defect, test/fixture defect, environment issue or unresolved. Explain supporting and contradicting evidence. Do not treat a passing retry as proof of a fix.
5. Propose the next discriminating check, or hand a supported diagnosis to the repair stage.

## Output contract

Return task_id, summary, source_anchors, findings, checks [{command,status}], open_questions. Use not-run for commands not executed. Keep the complete report within 12000 UTF-8 bytes and validate with the installed handoff helper. Schema validation is not truth verification.

## Boundaries

Read only assigned sources when delegated. Do not edit, push or expand scope without authorization. Escalate missing evidence. Keep full logs in approved local artifacts; admit only relevant excerpts.

## Operating resources and first-use setup

Before acting in a new repository, read [repository-setup.md](references/repository-setup.md) to bind actual commands, revision identity, allowed paths and CI tooling. Use native discovery appropriate to the harness: Claude slash invocation, Codex dollar skill mention, or the delivered OpenCode command/skill. If a required tool or permission is unavailable, report the gap; do not invent an execution result.

Use the [task and report contracts](references/contracts.md) and supplied [task](assets/task.json) / [report](assets/report.json) drafts. Replace draft markers and required checks before assessment. From this skill's directory, inspect `node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" --help`, then run the helpers using quoted absolute paths as needed. This skill carries its own helpers; it does not require a project framework.

```sh
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" validate-task /path/to/task.json
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" validate-report /path/to/report.json
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" assess /path/to/report.json --task /path/to/task.json
node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" handoff /path/to/report.json --task /path/to/task.json
```

Assessment binds required checks to the reviewed task. Exit 2 means declared evidence is incomplete; the helper does not run commands, authenticate, fetch CI, grant permission or establish factual truth. A wrong-revision result cannot become a passed check for the target in the bounded handoff. Reopen actual source/results when reviewing consequential claims.

## Read only the reference for this stage

- [diagnosis.md](references/diagnosis.md): failure classification, bounded repro and escalation.
- [evidence.md](references/evidence.md): honest statuses and source-linked output.

Before broad rollout, use [evaluation.md](references/evaluation.md) to test representative tasks, model suitability, actual native integration and accepted-task results. [provenance.md](references/provenance.md) records the published authoring patterns used; this package is original and carries no vendor certification.

## Two different report operations

Use scripts/qa.mjs with the full QA report and reviewed task to assess required-check coverage or generate a bounded handoff. A returned six-field worker report is validated directly with scripts/handoff.mjs; do not pass it as a full QA report. All helper paths belong to this skill and remain usable after the download is deleted. Commands in reference pages are relative to this skill directory; use the resolved absolute script path from a repository.

# Bind the workflow to this repository

Read this before executing a QA workflow in an unfamiliar repository. The package does not invent test commands, provision credentials or authorize remote actions.

## Establish the working boundary

1. Locate the repository root and current worktree. Read applicable native guidance before choosing commands or edit paths. Inspect `git status --short` and `git rev-parse HEAD`; preserve unrelated changes.
2. Read the relevant package/build manifest and test-runner configuration, not every repository file. Find the existing targeted test, fixtures and reporting conventions with bounded searches.
3. Identify the project's package manager and supported runtime from its lockfile/configuration. Use existing scripts and local tools. Do not silently install a global runner or substitute another framework.
4. Record the requested goal, allowed edit paths, acceptance constraints and required local/remote checks in a task packet. Resolve missing acceptance requirements before treating a result as complete.

Start from the installed `assets/task.json`. Replace its draft task/revision markers and configure actual commands. Run:

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-task task.json
```

Helper commands in this reference are relative to the installed skill directory. Keep the actual QA work in the repository and use a quoted absolute skill-helper path there. A workflow's input/output contracts remain the same across native harnesses; tool capabilities and permissions do not.

## Local execution profile

For Playwright, read the project's config and scripts first. The CLI supports targeted files, `--workers`, `--repeat-each` and reporters; the repository's own script may add required setup. Compare a bounded isolated run and parallel run only when that comparison addresses the hypothesis. Set an explicit repetition/time budget. Do not repeatedly run a failing suite without learning a new fact.

Record command, exit status, report path and the tested code identity. If tests ran on an uncommitted patch, record that fact and a patch/tree fingerprint. Before attributing those results to a later commit, establish that the committed tested files match, or rerun the relevant checks. Do not relabel a result with a new SHA merely because it is convenient.

## CI profile

Use the organization's installed, approved CI client. For GitHub Actions, read-only examples are:

```sh
gh pr checks PR_NUMBER --json name,state,link
gh run view RUN_ID --json status,conclusion,headSha,url,jobs
```

Inspect the run's `headSha`, required job conclusions and actual test report. Fetch a bounded relevant log excerpt when necessary; keep the full report in the approved evidence location. If a CLI field is unsupported, inspect the installed command's help/schema instead of guessing. Treat missing credentials, inaccessible logs and unsupported CI providers as explicit evidence gaps. Do not copy authentication output or secrets into the task report.

A request to investigate CI does not inherently authorize pushing, rerunning paid jobs, changing branch protection or deploying. Reuse existing authorization when it covers the concrete action. Otherwise prepare the diff/evidence before requesting the missing authorization. The task packet's action metadata records intent; it never grants native permissions.

## Native entry points

- Claude: invoke `/context-workflow`, `/qa-regression-repair` or `/qa-release-validation` when installed.
- Codex: invoke the corresponding `$context-workflow`, `$qa-regression-repair` or `$qa-release-validation` skill.
- OpenCode: use the delivered command wrapper where installed, or ask the agent to use the named skill.

Sources: [Playwright CLI](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli), [GitHub run inspection](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_view), [Claude skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), [Codex skills](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills).

# Task, evidence report and bounded handoff contracts

Run helpers from this skill directory (`node scripts/qa.mjs ...`) or through the installed skill's quoted absolute `scripts/qa.mjs` path. The latter and its supporting `handoff.mjs` allow a skill folder to remain usable independently of the project helper location.

## User-reviewed task packet

Copy [assets/task.json](../assets/task.json) and configure the actual task ID, goal, revision, allowed paths, required checks and repository commands. The draft revision marker is deliberately rejected until replaced. Required checks belong in this packet before assessment; a report cannot relax them by omission.

| Field                          | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `task_id`, `goal`, `revision`  | Stable task identity, requested outcome and actual target code identity                         |
| `classification_required`      | Whether a supported non-unresolved diagnosis is an acceptance requirement                       |
| `required_checks`              | Unique `{id, kind}` entries; `kind` is `local` or `ci`                                          |
| `constraints`, `allowed_paths` | User/repository constraints and approved edit scope                                             |
| `commands`                     | Repository-specific command strings or null when not configured; the helper never executes them |
| `external_actions`             | Push/deploy authorization metadata; never a permission grant                                    |

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-task task.json
```

## Full QA evidence report

Copy [assets/report.json](../assets/report.json). Keep the full report within 128 KiB; large logs and test reports stay in approved linked artifacts. Unknown top-level/nested fields and duplicate identifiers are rejected.

- `diagnosis` contains classification, summary and supporting/counterevidence IDs. Classification is product-defect, test-defect, environment-issue or unresolved. Referenced evidence IDs must exist; resolved diagnoses need support.
- `evidence` contains unique `{id, anchor, note}` entries. Anchors identify actual source lines, local artifacts or approved remote records. Exclude secrets and raw private histories.
- `checks` contains `{id, kind, revision, status, command, artifact, run_id, url}`. Status is passed, failed, pending, inaccessible or not-run. Passed checks require artifacts; passed CI checks also need run identity and a credential-free HTTPS URL. Use null for unavailable optional references, not invented values.
- `risks` records limitations; `open_work` records unfinished acceptance work. Do not remove a genuine open requirement merely to satisfy an automated gate.

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-report report.json
node scripts/qa.mjs assess report.json --task task.json
```

Assessment exit codes: 0 = declared coverage gate passed; 2 = valid input but incomplete/mismatched evidence; 1 = invalid input or invocation. This is not factual validation, artifact authenticity, CI execution, authorization or release approval. Reopen relevant primary results before accepting claims.

## Worker return

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs handoff report.json --task task.json
```

The generated return uses exactly `task_id`, `summary`, `source_anchors`, `findings`, `checks [{command,status}]`, `open_questions`, within the existing 12,000-byte serialized limit. It links the full report rather than embedding it. Incomplete statuses use not-run in the narrower worker vocabulary. Wrong-revision results cannot be advertised as passed for the target. Preserve the full report's more specific state and assessment reasons.

## Honest incomplete example

A report with local passed and CI pending is structurally valid but cannot pass a task that requires CI. A green CI job for another revision is also incomplete. Neither condition authorizes new remote activity; the coordinator uses existing approval or requests only the missing action after preparing the concrete work.

# Evaluate the installed package on representative work

## Validation layers

1. **Offline helper checks:** schema constraints, duplicate/unknown field rejection, revision binding, pending/inaccessible states, missing artifacts and bounded handoffs. These test deterministic behavior only.
2. **Skill application scenarios:** check whether an agent follows the intended decision gates and finds the relevant references. Baselines should reveal a concrete gap; avoid expanding instructions without an observed need.

Failing test/revision, fixture setup/teardown sources, worker topology and isolated-versus-parallel evidence.

## Review

1. Map resource ownership: who creates each user/cart/session, who mutates it and who cleans it up?
2. Identify shared IDs, static/global state, worker-scoped resources and cleanup that can affect another test.
3. Compare the fixture contract with product behavior before deciding which layer is defective.
4. Propose a deterministic competing-operation regression. A sleep or retry increase alone is not an evidence-based isolation fix.
5. Recommend the narrowest ownership change, including teardown safety and remaining risks.

## Output

Source-linked ownership table, candidate race/interference, counterevidence, proposed regression and unresolved questions. For delegated delivery use the installed six-field handoff contract and its byte bound. Report checks as passed, failed or not-run with actual evidence references in findings/source anchors.

Before acting in a new repository, read [repository-setup.md](references/repository-setup.md) to bind actual commands, revision identity, allowed paths and CI tooling. node "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/qa.mjs" validate-task /path/to/task.json


# Regression design

## Input contract

Supported hypothesis, affected source anchors, expected invariant, allowed edits and acceptance criteria.

## Design and execution

1. State the invariant and the counterexample that should fail before the fix.
2. Prefer deterministic synchronization/data setup over sleeps or probabilistic timing.
3. Add the smallest regression at the layer that owns the defect. Preserve relevant product contracts.
4. Run the regression before and after the scoped patch if execution is authorized. Record actual commands and results; otherwise label not-run.
5. Select related checks, parallel repeats and CI coverage that can catch collateral effects. Explain limitations and cost.

## Output

Regression rationale, changed paths, before/after evidence, required local/CI checks and unresolved risks. A passing local test is not a CI result. Keep revision identity with each test report.

Do not weaken assertions or inflate retries to hide a failure. Do not modify production code when only a test defect is supported. Ask for missing external-action authorization only after preparing the concrete diff and evidence.

State the supported behavior, triggering condition and observable violation. Link the source contract and failure evidence. Decide which layer owns the defect before choosing the test layer. # Reconcile evidence without overstating acceptance

The full QA report is an operational artifact. The bounded handoff is a summary with links. Neither is a substitute for reading the actual test/CI results.

## Evidence matrix

For every required check preserve its ID, kind (local/CI), exact tested revision, command or job, status and artifact. A passed CI check also needs a run ID and HTTPS result URL. Record retries/attempts rather than dropping failed attempts from the narrative. Do not include credentials, authorization headers or private session histories.

| Status       | Meaning                                                             | Completion consequence                              |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| passed       | An actual result supports this check for its recorded code identity | Eligible for declared coverage; verify the artifact |
| failed       | Actual execution found a failing check                              | Required acceptance remains incomplete              |
| pending      | A run/job has not finished                                          | Wait or checkpoint; never relabel passed            |
| inaccessible | Result cannot be inspected with current approved access             | Report the gap and next authorized retrieval path   |
| not-run      | Execution did not occur or is outside authorized/available scope    | Required acceptance remains incomplete              |

## Identity and coverage gates

Bind the report to a user-reviewed task packet with explicit required checks. The helper rejects malformed/duplicate IDs and missing passed-result artifacts; it flags missing checks, wrong revisions, unresolved required diagnosis and declared open acceptance work. A green result for another SHA cannot satisfy the target check. A report cannot declare completion simply by omitting a required check from itself.

`external_actions` in the task packet records authorization metadata only. The helper does not inspect native permissions, grant approval or execute commands. A structurally valid report can still contain false claims or stale links. The coordinator independently verifies supporting source/results and organizational acceptance requirements.

## Full report and bounded return

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs assess report.json --task task.json
node scripts/qa.mjs handoff report.json --task task.json
```

Assessment prints coverage status and reasons; exit 2 means incomplete declared evidence. The handoff uses the existing six-field worker contract and a 12,000-byte serialized bound. Pending/inaccessible checks become not-run in that reduced status vocabulary; the full report preserves their actual state. Reports from another revision must remain visibly unverified for the target.

## Handoff wording

Use a result such as: “Local targeted and parallel checks passed on the recorded patch. CI run X for target revision Y is pending; remote acceptance remains unverified.” If CI passes for Z instead, state the mismatch and retrieve the correct run. For release work, distinguish evidence readiness from deployment/release approval.

# Review resource ownership in parallel tests

Read the real test-runner configuration and repository fixture helpers. Do not assume that a fixture's name establishes its scope. In Playwright, distinguish test-scoped and worker-scoped fixtures and inspect setup/teardown dependencies; other frameworks use different lifetime rules.

## Ownership ledger

For each contested resource, record:

| Field            | Question                                                          |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identity         | Which user, cart, tenant, session, file or database key is used?  |
| Creator          | Which test/helper creates it, and with which unique namespace?    |
| Lifetime         | Is it per operation, test, worker, suite or external environment? |
| Mutators         | Can another test or worker modify the same identity?              |
| Cleanup          | Can teardown delete or reset state it does not own?               |
| Product contract | Does the product guarantee isolation for the supplied identity?   |

Trace the identity from setup through the product request and cleanup. Static variables, shared credentials, singleton sessions and broad cleanup queries are candidate signals, not automatic proof of a defect.

## Discriminating checks

- Compare isolated and concurrent runs on the same revision and environment.
- Make the suspected competing operation deterministic with a controlled barrier or explicit state setup where the framework permits it.
- Verify that unique test-owned resources remove the interference without weakening the intended product assertion.
- Check failure-path cleanup as well as success. Use the repository's existing lifecycle facilities; derive API/helper names from actual source.

Prefer a per-test ownership fix when the test contract requires independent mutable state. Worker-scoped immutable setup can be useful when mutation and cleanup boundaries are explicit. Do not isolate away a real product cross-tenant/data-leak defect: preserve a product-level regression if valid inputs violate that contract.

## Repair packet

Return the ownership ledger, conflicting source anchors, proposed fixture change, deterministic regression and limitations. Identify any existing test-data factory/setup conventions to reuse. Do not create speculative endpoint names or replace a framework merely to fit this protocol.

Verify targeted behavior, repeated parallel execution and relevant neighboring tests with a bounded budget. Record the tested revision/patch identity, actual reports and remaining environment differences. A successful sample does not prove the absence of all flakes.

Source: [Playwright fixtures and scope](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures). The ownership procedure above is an authored cross-framework review protocol; native configuration must be inspected in the target repository.

# Turn the diagnosis into a discriminating regression

## Define the acceptance invariant

State the supported behavior, triggering condition and observable violation. Link the source contract and failure evidence. Decide which layer owns the defect before choosing the test layer. A supported product defect may require product changes; an unsupported product theory does not expand a test-only authorization.

## Test design gate

The proposed regression should fail for the diagnosed reason before the fix and distinguish the corrected behavior afterward. Prefer controlled inputs, deterministic synchronization and resource ownership to arbitrary sleeps. Reuse the repository's test framework and fixtures. Do not weaken assertions, skip coverage or raise retries simply to obtain green output.

If the historical revision cannot be executed, report that limitation. A newly written passing test without a demonstrated failure is weaker evidence and must not be described as a verified regression. A flaky sample needs a bounded repetition strategy and explicit observed counts.

## Repair and inspect

1. Make the narrowest change that resolves the supported cause within allowed paths.
2. Inspect the diff for unrelated changes, weakened checks, cleanup hazards and compatibility effects.
3. Run the targeted regression and checks chosen for collateral risk. Use actual repository commands discovered during setup.
4. Keep the full report in the approved artifact store and admit a concise result into parent context. Failed diagnostic output remains intact when result bounding cannot safely apply.

## Revision-linked verification

Record the code identity actually tested. Distinguish an uncommitted worktree from its base HEAD. If a later commit changes the tested tree, rerun the relevant checks; if only packaging/commit metadata changes, retain evidence that the tested files match. Remote acceptance requires the CI run's tested revision and required job/test results, not just a green notification.

Use the shared task/report contracts to bind required checks before the report is assessed:

```sh
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-task task.json
node scripts/qa.mjs validate-report report.json
node scripts/qa.mjs assess report.json --task task.json
```

Exit 2 means declared evidence coverage is incomplete. It does not mean the program found the product defect or ran a test. Helpers never execute the command strings in reports.

## Stop and escalation

Stop speculative patching when the regression does not isolate the cause, authorized paths are insufficient, or new evidence contradicts the diagnosis. Report the conflict and next check. Do not hide unresolved failures in a completion summary or treat local success as CI acceptance.

# Coordinator stage gates

Read only the reference for the current stage. The coordinator can revisit a stage when new evidence changes the hypothesis; this is not an irreversible linear script.

| Stage              | Required input                                                  | Concrete output                                                      | Hold or revisit when                                           |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Scope              | User goal, permitted actions, relevant revision and constraints | Reviewed task packet, required-check IDs and selected source scope   | Acceptance or allowed edits are ambiguous                      |
| Diagnose           | Failure signature, bounded repro, fixture and product anchors   | Classification, supporting/counterevidence and falsifying regression | Evidence conflicts or no discriminating check exists           |
| Repair             | Supported hypothesis, allowed paths and regression design       | Minimal patch, diff review and regression evidence                   | Patch exceeds authorization or the regression misses the cause |
| Local verification | Actual patch identity and repository commands                   | Targeted/parallel/related command results and artifacts              | Required local checks fail, are unavailable or were not run    |
| CI verification    | Reviewed patch, applicable push authorization, target revision  | Actual run/job results for that revision                             | Run is pending, inaccessible, wrong-revision or failed         |
| Handoff            | Verified evidence matrix and explicit coverage limits           | Full report, bounded summary, checkpoint/open work                   | Required evidence or acceptance remains incomplete             |

## Worker coordination

Assign bounded read-only tasks that can be reviewed independently: CI failure extraction, fixture/product ownership critique or verification-report review. Give exact files/anchors and expected return fields. Do not give every worker the full parent history. Parent owns edits, tests, source reconciliation and acceptance. Model choice follows task difficulty and evidence quality; escalate uncertainty. Model availability and quality need native validation.

Validate report structure before admitting it. Reopen primary source anchors when claims conflict or affect acceptance. A successful helper validation is not a successful test. Include worker calls and repeated prefixes when evaluating cost; parallel work does not automatically reduce all-call input.

## Session boundaries

Before compaction or a deliberate handoff, preserve current goal, applicable constraints, source/revision anchors, decisions, required checks and unfinished work. The selected PreCompact hook supplies guidance; it does not generate a factual checkpoint itself. Validate the checkpoint and restore selected facts after the boundary. Native auto-compaction remains the base harness's responsibility and timing is version-dependent.

## External actions and recovery

Reuse existing authorization that covers the concrete action. If absent, prepare the diff/results before asking. Do not push, rerun paid infrastructure, deploy or alter permissions merely because a skill requests a stage. On interruption, leave a checkpoint with exact pending run/revision IDs. Resume by verifying that the goal, branch/worktree and CI state still match; stale checkpoints cannot override current user intent.
